newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor at low after plant mothballing report.
newsitem.headline: Iscor at low after plant mothballing report.

text.p: Shares in South African iron and steel producer Iscor Ltd fell to a new 1997 low following reports that it was considering mothballing its Pretoria steel mill, so endangering 1,400 jobs.
By 0740 GMT Iscor had shed seven cents to 280 cents, dipping further on its 286 cents low set on Monday.
Dealers said that the international steel market was still very flat and that Iscor had been falling steadily since late last month.
"Their results for the year to June 30 are also not expected to be good," a dealer said.

Business Day newspaper said earlier that Iscor was considering stopping operations at the plant as it had failed to climb out of the red, despite bids to cut costs and change to stainless steel production.
A decision on whether the plant would be permanently shut, mothballed or continued under a more stringent cost-cutting scenario would be made in the next few weeks, the paper said.
But dealers said Iscor was beginning to show value at these low levels.
"We think that below 280 cents people will again see buying potential," a dealer said.
